Excellent communication with the vet. I took my dog ​​in today and I already think she's doing better. I highly recommend her.

Superb, both of you! A while ago, my cat got into a fight with another cat outside. His paw got infected; it swelled up to his chest. I was terrified. He wasn't neutered either. She suggested neutering him since he's a cat who goes outside every day, sometimes for several days at a time. For several reasons, which were perfect for me, I thought it would cost me over €300 between the consultation, leaving him there to treat his arm, the neutering, and the medication. But not at all! She was incredibly accommodating, putting him under for the neutering at the same time as the arm treatment. And frankly, it didn't even cost me half that. With the treatments, their kindness, understanding, and gentleness, I've rarely seen anything like it. I had gone to the SPA (animal shelter) in La Valentine just before, and they gave me a very cold reception, looking down their noses at me as soon as I... I got home, etc. The price was incredible, thank you so much to this team.
Ms. Rascle is very kind and wonderful; she explains things very well. I highly recommend her.

I wanted to leave a sincere review here, with no overcharging or unnecessary treatments offered just to boost sales. She is exceptionally honest, explains everything clearly, and always prioritizes the animal's health. She is incredibly patient and gentle with my cat, who is quite timid. He leaves each visit feeling relaxed! Professionalism, kindness, and transparency: everything you could want in a veterinarian. Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

Warning to all pet owners: Avoid!

I went to Veterinary Clinic Le Merlan because they are the regular vet for my two pets. Three days after an emergency visit (for veal bones my dog ​​had ingested), I brought my dog ​​back because he was complaining of stomach pain. The consultation cost €35, but no further examinations (no x-rays, no ultrasound, no blood work) were performed.

Even worse, the vet left me extremely stressed by offering vague hypotheses: "maybe muscular, maybe neurological, maybe the beginning of an epileptic seizure," without providing a clear diagnosis or suggesting any tests. The next day, on a friend's advice, I went to the Clinique de la Valentine: they performed further examinations (x-rays) and prescribed the correct treatment. Thanks to their care, my dog ​​is doing much better.

Even though it's my regular vet, I'll never set foot in that clinic again. In my opinion, the diagnosis wasn't done properly, and the proposed treatment wasn't appropriate; worse still, it could have made things worse. Veterinarian Le Merlan isn't what it used to be.

This is my honest feedback. A word to the wise!
